text:
kevin: Heads-up — thinking about a pattern for strict per-tenant telemetry isolation. Proposal: tokenized exporter keys so collectors only forward spans to tenant-owned sinks. Wanted quick sync before I write an RFC.
priya: +1 curious about how this intersects with cross-tenant traces for infra (eg sidecar->platform).
kevin: Good call. I was thinking tenant token on span attribute e.g. tenant.id, collector enforces that exporter key must match tenant.id. If missing -> route to quarantine export or drop.
alex: That sounds safe but how do we avoid schema explosion in exporters? We can't maintain N exporter configs for every tenant in the collector.
maria: Could do dynamic exporter provisioning with a single generic HTTP exporter that signs to downstream with per-tenant creds. Collector keeps a map of token->credentials. That avoids static exporters.
sam: Concern: sampling and aggregation. If we silo fully, we lose cross-tenant service-level metrics. We still need aggregated infra telemetry for global SLOs.
eva: Maybe two-tier routing: spans with tenant.id -> per-tenant sink. Spans without tenant.id but from infra namespace -> infra sink. Or duplicate critical infra spans to both per-tenant and infra aggregate (configurable, sampled).
priya: Also RBAC: product/customer support should only be able to query their dataset. We need enforcement in both storage and query layer, not just routing. Routing goodies are necessary but not sufficient.
kevin: Agreed. Routing is the first line of defense. Storage must tag entries and ACLs applied at read time. But routing reduces blast radius and egress cost.
ops-bot: deploy-check — collector feature flag "tenant-token-routing" enabled in staging.
alex: For sensitive data, we should run PII scrubbing in the collector before routing. That allows you to redact before it lands in tenant-managed sinks.
maria: We can plug a processing step that strips specific attributes or masks values using regex/lookup policies. Will add perf notes — processing adds CPU cost per span.
sam: Cost tradeoff: per-tenant retention policies will increase storage ops complexity. How do we let customers choose retention without exploding indices?
eva: Use a single time-series/storage bucket with tenant_id tag and lifecycle rules that GC by tenant. Many backends (e.g., Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, BigQuery) support retention based on partition key.
kevin: Example collector routing pseudo-config I prototyped:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  tenantsplit:
    attribute: tenant.id
    default_exporter: quarantine
exporters:
  http_generic:
    endpoint: https://exporter-proxy.internal/tenant/{{tenant.id}}/ingest
  quarantine:
    endpoint: https://telemetry-quarantine.internal/ingest
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [tenantsplit]
      exporters: [http_generic, quarantine]
```
priya: That dynamic endpoint with templating is neat. How do we secure that exporter-proxy? It needs to verify the token and sign to downstream.
maria: The proxy would hold tenant creds (KMS/HSM-backed). Collector sends tenant token in header, proxy verifies and signs to downstream sink. Collector never holds long-lived sink creds.
alex: Edge-case: SDKs that don't set tenant.id or older clients — we need fallback route, alerting, and automatic backfill if we can correlate.
sam: Backfill is tricky. We could correlate by API key used at ingress and retroactively tag spans, but that requires keeping raw untagged spans for a short TTL in quarantine.
eva: Also need to think about evals and rollouts: when we A/B change exporter config, how do we avoid data loss? Canary route a small percentage and monitor.
kevin: Agreed. Add rollout policies: percentage-based split, or header-based canary. Collector feature flags for safe rollout.
ops-bot: perf-alert — tenantsplit processor increases p50 trace latency by ~2ms in staging (10k reqs).
maria: 2ms is acceptable if we batch and use async forwarding. But need to budget CPU for peak token validation.
priya: For RBAC in the console, we'll map tenant_id -> org in our authz system. Query API enforces tenant scope. Also need SSO mapping.
kevin: One more: cross-tenant traces where a request flows through a shared infra component (eg auth service). Should we duplicate those spans to each tenant involved?
alex: I think span duplication for multi-tenant requests makes sense for debugging, but mark them specially (shared:true) and don't count them against per-tenant quota.
sam: Quota enforcement: tokenized exporters allow us to throttle per-tenant at ingress. Good for DoS protection.
eva: Long-term: consider a hybrid approach — push critical traces to tenant-owned sinks, but keep low-sample aggregated metrics centrally for infra SLOs.
kevin: OK next steps: I will write RFC covering: collector templated exporters, token lifecycle (rotate/revoke), quarantine TTL and backfill plan, PII scrubbers, rollout strategy, storage ACLs, and console RBAC mapping. Folks who want to pair — @priya @maria please.
priya: I'll take token lifecycle + console RBAC mapping.
maria: I'll own collector processors + PII scrubbers and perf tests.
alex: I'll take aggregate infra metrics plan and sampling config.
sam: I'll draft quota/ingress throttling + retention cost model.
eva: I'll help with rollout/canary and multi-tenant duplication semantics.
kevin: Thanks all. Will post RFC draft next week. Closing loop: ops-bot please keep feature flag >staging until we've validated retention and perf.
ops-bot: noted — feature flag "tenant-token-routing" remains enabled in staging until 1775439999 or manual toggle.
